## Enrich Eligibility
Reads roles still marked eligibility=unknown, ordered by eligibility_checked_at ASC NULLS FIRST so never-checked rows go first and the backlog drains (ordering by fit_score starved low-ranked rows: un-fetchable high scorers were re-picked every run).

Pick Batch keeps only PRIMARIES (dedup_group null or = id) — the app displays primaries only, so grading a duplicate spends a Groq call on an invisible row and can leave a blocker on the hidden copy while the visible primary stays unknown.

It also skips rows checked within the last 14 days. An 'unknown' verdict leaves the row in the pool, so without that guard every run would re-grade the same rows forever once the backlog is empty. The 14-day window still lets a future JD-fetching improvement (JSON-LD for Workday/iCIMS) sweep through and upgrade them.

Fetches the job description (Greenhouse/Lever only — Workday/iCIMS return JS, not text), then one LLM call: hard blockers = citizenship/clearance, Master/PhD required, a required language not held (C++/Java/Go/etc), or an explicit J-1 exclusion / F-1-CPT-only rule. NOT blockers = merely not offering sponsorship (J-1 AT self-authorizes), Rust, preferred skills.

Writes eligibility + reason + jd_text + eligibility_checked_at on EVERY pass, including unknown verdicts.

KNOWN LIMIT: non-primaries are never stamped, so they sit permanently at the front of the read window. Harmless at ~9 of 120; revisit if duplicates exceed ~30% of the read limit.
